title: wiretap: De-duplicate file-opening code.
description:
Reduce code duplication by restructuring the code for walking through the list
of potential file types when opening a file, rolling up six instances of
near-identical code into one.  Behavior should be unchanged by this commit.

While we're here, fix a trivial typo in wiretap/README.developer .

notes.body:
added 11 commits
  • 7e087176...7759efe6 - 10 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • a63f5fc8 - wiretap: De-duplicate file-opening code.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/16393/diffs?diff_id=1063571284&start_sha=7e087176f78368251a1cd390fb593437927c59a1)

Coverity suggests that this should be
`*candidates = g_malloc(sizeof **candidates);`

(and similar for line 792)

In practice, on all the platforms we actively support, if ''X'' is of pointer to pointer to pointer type, `sizeof *X` and `sizeof **X` are the same, as `*X` and `**X` are both pointers and all pointers are the same type on those platforms, but we shouldn't count on that.

I.e., the code happens to work, but should be fixed.  Perhaps `g_new()` should be used.
Or perhaps do it as a `GPtrArray`, given that it returns a variable-sized array of pointers.

Ah, let me investigate the `GPtrArray` option.

I thought I had gotten all my pointer types correct but now I can see clearly that I was quite mistaken.  There was an intermittent stage of coding where `candidates` was a `struct open_info **candidates`, at which time `sizeof *candidates` would have been correct, but it ended up "correct" only because `sizeof **candidates` is the same as `sizeof *candidates`, which is as good as being incorrect...

I'll get it fixed today.  Thanks for the heads-up!
See !16407 for a change to use `GPtrArray`.  Thanks again for the feedback!
